reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh independent audit instance
findings: Receipt fingerprint, implementation digest, all three implementation-file hashes and all 26 provenance inputs independently match. Fresh SHA-256 of the bound live llama-server binary reproduces 5719c246ec3622ea1df3c3f498075879f12f1f70b969f8b591e87b3a1f3c8808.

The bound pre-route snapshot has exactly four idle speculative slots 0 through 3, and ExecStart fixes the same binary, Fable-TC model path, four-slot context and --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4. PID 29428, ExecStart, binary hash, zero restarts and both health endpoints remain unchanged.

All 100 retained rows form exactly 25 complete four-slot rounds with unique round/slot keys and identical frozen request settings. Every physical response id_slot equals its requested slot, all responses stop naturally, and the four distinct baseline contents are reproduced byte-for-byte in all 96 non-baseline repetitions.

Independent scoring reproduces exact-repeat 100/100, own nonce 100/100 and zero foreign nonce occurrences. Each slot returns only its assigned content across all 25 rounds; excluding the trivially self-matching baseline round leaves the same 96/96 repeat result.

Every response reports real speculative work: draft_n ranges 8 to 16 and accepted drafts 3 to 7. Totals independently reproduce 1,308 proposed, 478 accepted and 830 rejected draft tokens; all 100 requests reject at least one draft.

Receipt-bound service logs corroborate explicit selected-slot IDs, overlapping launches on slots 0 through 3, draft-acceptance counts and clean releases. The final /slots snapshot contains four speculative, non-processing slots and preserves the frozen request parameters.

Adversarial false-positive audit notes that each nonce is present in its own prompt and therefore nonce success alone is weak. Prompt-cache reuse is also uneven across slots. Neither fact explains away the stronger physical-slot response binding, concurrent log evidence, 830 rollback events, exact per-slot repetitions and clean recovery, but they prohibit claims about cache persistence or internal pointer transactions.

Approval is strictly limited to observable live slot isolation for this exact binary, model route, deterministic short prompts and four-slot draft-MTP runtime. It does not validate the historical Python manager's microsecond overhead, internal pointer atomicity, long-context cache isolation, stochastic decoding, semantic workload quality or general production readiness.
